thread:
Maria - Design: Quick pass — on phones the console table gets super cramped at 720px. I prototyped turning the rows into stacked cards and the sidebar into a bottom-sheet. Thoughts?
Jamal - Eng: I saw that. Cards feel nicer than tiny columns, but we need to decide what to keep visible on the card header (status, name, primary action?)
Alex - Product: Priority is scanning: name, status, last updated. Actions can be in a chevron overflow. Keep ID off the main header.
Maria - Design: Agreed. Header: title, status chip, timestamp. Secondary details (ID, region, model) in collapsible section.
Sam - Accessibility: Bottom-sheet must trap focus and restore focus to the triggering element when closed. Also ensure aria-expanded on the row button.
Jamal - Eng: Implementation notes: we already have a drawer component. Could reuse it, but the drawer is anchored to the side. Need variant for full-width bottom-sheet with swipe to close and keyboard escape.
Lin - PM: One UX question — should the sidebar collapse into a bottom-sheet (overlay) or a persistent mini rail? Mobile first I think overlay makes more sense to maximize space.
Maria - Design: Overlay bottom-sheet wins for quick context. Persistent mini-rail feels cramped and nonstandard on phones.
Jamal - Eng: Two engineering cautions: 1) table virtualization breaks when rows convert to variable-height cards, performance hit; 2) we must avoid layout shifts when virtual keyboard opens on iOS.
Maria - Design: Good point. We can set a max-height on the sheet and enable internal scrolling. Also add safe-area padding.
Sam - Accessibility: Make sure the sheet content uses role="dialog" and has aria-modal="true". Announce the title with aria-labelledby. For screen reader users, the sheet shouldn't push main content — mark main as aria-hidden while open.
Jamal - Eng: CSS snippet I tested for the sheet:
```css
.sheet {
  position: fixed;
  inset: auto 0 0 0;
  max-height: 85vh;
  border-top-left-radius: 12px;
  border-top-right-radius: 12px;
  -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
}
```
Maria - Design: Nice. Also thinking about table overflow on mid-width (tablet). Instead of card switch at 720px, maybe add a compact row at 840px and only switch to cards below 560px. That avoids frequent flipping.
Alex - Product: Sounds reasonable. Data: 60% of active sessions are phones with width < 480, 25% tablets. So cards below 600 would capture phones and small phablets.
Jamal - Eng: Proposal: breakpoints: >=960 desktop table, 600-959 compact table (hide low-priority cols, horizontal scroll on overflow), <600 cards + bottom-sheet detail.
Maria - Design: I like the three-tier approach. For compact table we should pin primary column (name) and allow action column to collapse into a kebab menu.
Sam - Accessibility: Horizontal scrolling tables are tricky. If we keep keyboard access to hidden columns via a show-more control, that's better than forcing a scroll. Maybe a "Show columns" menu.
Lin - PM: Copy tweak request: on rows that expand, use "View details" rather than "Expand" — clearer for non-technical users.
Maria - Design: Noted. Also change the bottom-sheet close affordance to an explicit "Done" button plus swipe area.
Jamal - Eng: I'll prototype a performance-friendly card list: simple static list up to 50 items, then enable incremental loading. Also keep virtualization for desktop/tablet.
ui-bot: deploy-preview created: https://deploys.company/preview/54928 (visual + accessibility checklist)
Maria - Design: Thanks. Can people test on iPhone 12 and Pixel 4 emulators for keyboard behavior? @Jamal @Sam
Jamal - Eng: Yep, I'll spin up a branch and drop screenshots.
Sam - Accessibility: I'll run the a11y checks and do a quick VoiceOver/ TalkBack pass.
Maria - Design: Great. If no objections I'll update the mock and push to Figma tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Alex - Product: No objections. Let's capture the breakpoints in the product doc and call this ready for engineering.
